correctness.rationale: Gaussian projection reduces risk to a quadratic kernel energy plus noise. Cauchy–Schwarz eliminates the precisions with equality for allocation proportional to absolute weight, leaving the squared l1 penalty divided by P; compact sites and uniform coercivity in the weights give a minimizer. For distinct active sites the Markov interpolation integrates to a strictly positive vector Qb, with Q=K_T^{-1}. The inverse of the Stieltjes matrix I+N^(1/2)QN^(1/2) is entrywise nonnegative with positive diagonal, so the noisy weights are strictly positive for every active set. Aggregate coincident readings by adding precisions. At an active endpoint the inward variation strictly decreases the energy; at any distinct interior site a symmetric split gains λw²ε+O(ε²) while leaving the noise penalty unchanged. These exclude endpoints and unused or duplicate sites and give strict improvement with an additional site. On each open gap the residual solves r''−λ²r=−2λ, with r(t_i)=c=Σw/P; the average of one-sided site slopes vanishes and the jump is 2λw_i. Hence adjacent weights coincide, the inner gaps coincide, and the two Robin boundary conditions give equal margins and the stated weight equation. Its sides are strictly monotone in opposite directions, so existence plus uniqueness of the root proves global optimality. At g=d the sign of the difference is the sign of P−n. The separate n=1 case is maximization of the positive kernel mean at 1/2. Evaluating the normal equations gives the stated risk and geometric sum.
residual_risks: The gap transition is for n≥2, where d is defined; the single midpoint always has two equal boundary margins. The symbolic checks are not the proof for arbitrary designs. Results concern deterministic sites, known covariance, and continuously divisible precision.

evidence: The first catalog record gives exact all-n noiseless OU nodes; the second gives exact noisy two-site nodes under a common noise variance. The remaining analogues give all-n precision allocation for Brownian motion and Brownian bridge. Cai et al. prove noisy quadrature complexity bounds; the available Mukherjee integral-estimation description does not state the claimed result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Noiseless design is a limiting case, fixed equal noise is a smaller feasible set for two sites, and the Wiener/bridge kernels do not have the exponential residual differential equation and Robin normalization used here.

evidence: At n=2 put η=2/P and s=λd/2; the frozen mesh equation becomes exp(λ/2)=exp(s)+(1+η)exp(2s)sinh(s), exactly the fixed-noise catalog root. At P→∞ it gives g=d/2+λ^(-1)log cosh(λd/2), hence exactly the earlier noiseless equation. Karvonen et al. treat positivity for locally optimized designs in a broader kernel framework.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both matching reductions are one-way. Free allocation changes the weight equations through a common residual level; positive weights alone do not prove it is best to spend precision at n distinct sites or that the global mesh obeys the finite-P equation.

originality.rationale: The assessed distinction is the finite-P, all-n free allocation theorem. The exact noiseless design and the fixed-equal-variance two-site geometry, risk and transition are already covered by indexed records. Neither includes the all-n optimization over freely allocated precisions, the finite-budget margin law for n≥3, or strict improvement in sensor count at fixed total precision. Other primary passages give the quadrature/energy framework, weight positivity, error rates, or different OU criteria; they do not supply this joint-design theorem.
residual_risks: The older integral-estimation dissertation section was not accessible; an equivalent treatment in older optimal-design literature remains possible. Same-day order of the restricted two-site theorem and this record is not established. The priority assessment only covers the checked differences.

value.rationale: The all-n result resolves whether it is preferable to concentrate a fixed sensing budget or spread it among extra sites: the exponential cusp strictly favors splitting and the global mesh is computable by one scalar root. The co-variation of boundary margins with budget and the exact P=n transition for n≥3 are useful predictions beyond the already solved noiseless and two-site regimes.
residual_risks: The transition and strict gain rely on the stated exponential covariance and continuously adjustable precision; integer replication costs could change the design.
